pm_exper_user_657_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I stop feeling burnt out from always being the one in my community group who ends up handling complicated forms and organizing the budget because no one else wants to do it?
pm_exper_user_657_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) It might help to set clearer boundaries with your group, letting them know that while you value contributing your skills, you can only take on certain tasks occasionally to avoid feeling overextended. Encouraging shared responsibility can prevent burnout for everyone.
(b) Consider offering short guidance sessions or templates instead of doing all the work yourself, similar to how you wish your family would approach you for advice rather than full responsibility for their bureaucratic and financial issues. This keeps you involved without exhausting you.
(c) It might help to set clearer boundaries with your community group, letting them know that while you value contributing your data skills, you can only take on certain tasks occasionally to avoid the same burnout you’ve felt in your family when handling their paperwork and financial matters.
(d) You could suggest rotating the budgeting and form-filling duties so you're not in the same position as with your relatives, where you're expected to be the default problem-solver because of your data literacy. That way, others can build confidence and share the load.
